title: Diamond and Suslin trees: prediction and construction
summary: Diamond implies the continuum hypothesis and supplies the predictions needed to construct a Suslin tree.
abstract: Diamond asserts that a single sequence can anticipate every subset of the first uncountable ordinal, by making one guess for each countable initial segment. For every subset, the correct guesses must occur within every closed unbounded set: a set reaching arbitrarily far and containing its limit points below that ordinal. Assuming diamond, the real line has the same size as the set of countable ordinals, and there is a Suslin tree. Such a tree has one level for every countable ordinal, yet every chain of comparable nodes and every antichain of mutually incomparable nodes is countable.
